# How to Find Any Indian Company’s Details in 2 Minutes


November 27, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/how-to-find-any-indian-companys-details-in-2-minutes/#respond)


**Short answer:** the quickest way to find any Indian company’s details is to search it on[Business Graph by Compose1](https://compose1.ai/apps/business-graph/) , a free business search tool. Type the company’s name, GST number, CIN, website or even a description like “furniture makers in Jodhpur”, and in under 2 minutes you’ll see its address, GST status, company registration, key people and connected businesses on one page. For official confirmation, you can cross-check on the free MCA and GST government portals.


It usually starts with a small doubt. A new supplier sends their first invoice. A candidate’s CV lists a company you’ve never heard of. A customer wants 60 days of credit. Before you say yes, you want to know one thing: is this business real, and is it who it says it is?


Ten years ago that meant a call to your CA. Today, everything you need is public. The trick is knowing where to look, and not wasting 20 minutes jumping between three government websites and fighting captchas. Here’s the 2-minute way, plus the official free methods for when you need them.


### What details can you find about an Indian company?


**Detail** **What it tells you** **Where it comes from**


Legal name and trade name The official name behind the brand on the signboard GST and MCA records


GSTIN and GST status Whether it’s registered for GST and still active GST records


CIN or LLPIN and company status Whether it’s a registered company or LLP, and if it’s active or struck off MCA records


Registration date How long the business has existed GST and MCA records


Type of business Proprietorship, partnership, private limited, LLP and so on GST and MCA records


Registered and business address Where it’s based, and whether that matches what they told you GST and MCA records


Directors and key people Who runs it, and what else they run MCA records


Website and connected businesses Its online presence and related companies Business Graph


One thing many guides miss: most Indian businesses aren’t companies at all. Shops, traders, contractors and small service firms are usually proprietorships or partnerships. They never appear on the MCA portal, but they do have a GST registration if they’re above the GST limit. A good search has to cover both.


#### The 2-minute method: search on Business Graph


[Business Graph](https://compose1.ai/apps/business-graph/) is a free search engine for Indian businesses, made by Compose1. It brings GST and company registration records together, so one search covers both companies and GST-registered proprietors and partnerships.


1. **Open Business Graph (10 seconds).** Go to the Business Graph search page and create a free account if you don’t have one.
2. **Type what you know (20 seconds).** A name, brand, GSTIN, CIN, PAN, pincode, website or product all work. You can even describe the business in plain words, like “CCTV installers in Nagpur”.
3. **Pick the right result (20 seconds).** Use the city and address to choose the right business when names are similar.
4. **Read the company page (60 seconds).** Check its addresses, websites, key people, GST and company registration details, and the other businesses it’s connected to.


That’s it. If the GST status is active, the name matches your invoice or CV, and the address makes sense, you’re good to go. If something looks off, use the red flags list further down.


**Why it’s faster:** the government portals make you know the exact name or number and solve a captcha for every search, and each portal shows only its own records. Business Graph lets you search loosely, like you’d search Google, and shows everything in one place. You can also run a search straight from the[Compose1 home page](https://compose1.ai/) .


## Other free ways to find company details


#### 1. MCA portal (for companies and LLPs)


The Ministry of Corporate Affairs portal is the official record for private and public limited companies, one person companies and LLPs.


1. Go to mca.gov.in and open MCA Services.
2. Choose the master data option (“View Company/LLP Master Data”).
3. Enter the company name or CIN and solve the captcha. You may be asked to sign in with a free MCA account.
4. Read the master data: CIN, status, registration date, registered address, capital and directors.


**Good for:** official confirmation of a company’s status and directors. **Limits:** companies and LLPs only, one search at a time, and you need a fairly exact name. Filed documents such as balance sheets cost a small fee.


#### 2. GST portal “Search Taxpayer” (for any GST-registered business)


1. Go to gst.gov.in, open Search Taxpayer and choose “Search by GSTIN/UIN”.
2. Enter the 15-character GSTIN and solve the captcha. No login is needed.
3. Check the legal name, trade name, registration date, constitution of business, status and principal place of business.


**Good for:** checking a vendor’s GSTIN before you pay an invoice. **Limits:** you need the exact GSTIN, and it only shows GST data. For a quicker GSTIN check, you can also use SalaryBox’s free[GST number search tool](https://salarybox.in/gst-number-search/) .


#### 3. Google, the company website and LinkedIn


Useful for a feel of the business: reviews, photos, team size and how active they are. But anyone can make a website or a LinkedIn page, so treat this as background, never as proof that a business is registered.


### Which method should you use?


**Method** **Time** **What you need to know** **Covers proprietors and partnerships?** **Cost**


[Business Graph](https://compose1.ai/apps/business-graph/) About 2 minutes Anything: name, GSTIN, CIN, website, or plain words Yes, through GST records Free to view


MCA portal 5 to 10 minutes Exact company name or CIN No Free (documents paid)


GST portal 3 to 5 minutes Exact GSTIN Yes Free


Google and LinkedIn Varies The name Sometimes Free


#### Real situations where a 2-minute check saves you


- **Onboarding a new vendor.** Check that the GSTIN on their invoice is active and belongs to the same business, so your input tax credit isn’t at risk. Our guide to[vendor management for Indian SMEs](https://salarybox.in/vendor-management-best-practices-for-indian-smes/) covers the rest of the process.
- **Verifying a candidate’s previous employer.** Search the employer’s name. Is it real, active and in the city the candidate mentioned? Did it exist during the years on the CV? It’s one of the simplest steps in[employee background verification](https://salarybox.in/blog/how-do-companies-conduct-employee-background-verification-in-india/) .
- **Giving credit to a new customer.** A business registered last month asking for 90-day terms deserves a closer look.
- **Hiring through a staffing agency or contractor.** Make sure the agency is registered and active before you hand over payroll for contract workers.
- **Preparing for a sales meeting.** Know who runs the business and what else they own before you walk in.


#### Red flags to watch for


- **GST status is “Cancelled” or “Suspended”.** Don’t pay GST to a business that can’t pass it on.
- **Company status is “Strike Off” or “Under process of striking off”.** The company is closed or closing.
- **The name doesn’t match.** The legal name on the GST record should match the name on the invoice or contract.
- **The address is somewhere else.** A Mumbai vendor whose GST address is in another state needs a good explanation.
- **Very new, very big claims.** A business registered a few months ago claiming “15 years of experience” is worth a second look.
- **No record at all.** A business above the GST limit with no GST registration and no company record is a warning sign.


##### Frequently asked questions


###### How can I find details of any company in India for free?


The fastest free way is Business Graph by Compose1: type the company’s name, GSTIN, CIN, website or even a description like “printing press in Indore”, and you get its address, GST and company registration details and key people on one page. You can also use the MCA portal for registered companies and the GST portal for any GST-registered business.


###### How do I check if a company is registered in India?


Search the company on Business Graph or the MCA portal. A private or public limited company or LLP will have a CIN or LLPIN and a status such as Active or Strike Off. Many small businesses are proprietorships or partnerships with no MCA record, so also check whether they have an active GST registration.


###### Can I find company details using a GST number?


Yes. Enter the GSTIN on Business Graph or on the GST portal’s “Search Taxpayer” page. You’ll see the legal name, trade name, registration date, type of business, principal place of business and whether the registration is active or cancelled. Business Graph also links that GSTIN to the company’s other details and key people.


###### How can I find the directors of a company in India?


Business Graph shows the key people of a business on its page. On the MCA portal, the company’s master data lists its directors along with their DIN. Directors’ personal contact details are not public, so reach them through the company’s official phone, email or website.


###### Is it legal to look up a company’s details?


Yes. Company registration and GST details are public so that anyone can check who they are dealing with. Use them to verify vendors, customers, employers and partners. Personal details of people, such as a director’s mobile number, are protected under India’s DPDP Act, so don’t collect or share them without a valid reason.


###### How do I verify a job candidate’s previous employer?


Search the employer’s name on Business Graph. Check that it exists, is active and is based where the candidate says. If it’s a registered company, the MCA status and registration date should match the years the candidate claims to have worked there. Then confirm employment with the company’s HR.

You can search by name, brand, GSTIN, CIN, PAN, pincode, website, product or plain words, and see a business’s addresses, websites, key people, GST and company registration details and connected businesses on one page. It also has an API.


#### The bottom line


Checking a business used to be a job for your CA. Now it takes 2 minutes and costs nothing. Make it a habit before you pay a new vendor, hire from an unknown company or extend credit to a new customer. It’s the cheapest protection your business will ever have.
